The single-agent era of AI is ending.

Anthropic just released **Dynamic Workflows** for Claude Code — a system that generates orchestration scripts on demand, spins up parallel agents, validates their work, and converges on a final solution.

**Why this matters:**
Most real engineering problems are too large for one agent. Codebase-wide migrations. Security audits across hundreds of files. Performance reviews of complex systems.

Dynamic Workflows split these across sub-agents, verify outputs, and iterate until results align.

**How it works:**
Claude automatically builds a workflow harness that plans tasks, runs subtasks in parallel, cross-checks results, and repeats until outputs converge.

Tasks that once required multi-quarter engineering effort can now be executed in days.

**The bigger shift:**
AI is becoming workflow-centric, not model-centric.

The key question is no longer "How smart is the model?" — it's "How well can a system of agents coordinate?"

This validates what we've been building at ByteStreams: AI should be a system, not a single agent. Verification and orchestration are the real unlocks.
